title: Warehouse Bond Management and Enforcement
summary: This thread covers the statutory framework for warehouse bonds, including registration, monitoring, and enforcement of government dues. The core legal procedures for managing bond registers and recovering unpaid duties remain consistent across the original Customs Act and its subsequent iterations.

evolution.legal_basis: Remains anchored in the Customs Act, 1969, with bilingual (English/Bengali) versions maintaining identical procedural requirements.

timeline.change: Codified the fundamental procedures for bond registration, duty recovery, and enforcement against defaulting warehouse owners.

১১২। শুল্ক, ইত্যাদি পরিশোধে ব্যর্থতার জন্য পদ্ধতি।— (১) যদি কোন মালিক ধারা ১১১ এর অধীন দাবীকৃত কোন অর্থ পরিশোধ করিতে ব্যর্থ হন, তাহা হইলে যথাযথ কর্মকর্তা ধারা ৮৬ এর অধীন সম্পাদিত বন্ডের উপর অথবা এই আইনের অধীন প্রণীত বিধিমালায় যেরূপ নির্ধারিত থাকে সেইরূপ কার্যক্রম গ্রহণ করিতে পারিবেন অথবা ওয়্যারহাউসে সংরক্ষিত মালিকের পণ্য অথবা পণ্য প্রস্তুতকরণে ব্যবহৃত কোন কারখানা, যন্ত্রপাতি অথবা মেশিনারীজ অথবা উক্ত ব্যক্তির মালিকানাধীন অন্য কোন পণ্য এবং সম্পত্তির এমন অংশ যাহা দাবী আদায়ের জন্য পর্যাপ্ত বিবেচিত হয় তাহা আটক করাইতে পারিবেন, এবং অবিলম্বে উক্তরূপ আটকের লিখিত নোটিশ মালিককে প্রদান করিতে হইবে।
(২) এই নোটিশের তারিখ হইতে পনের দিবসের মধ্যে দাবী পূরণ করা না হইলে উক্তরূপ আটককৃত পণ্য বিক্রয় করা যাইবে।
(৩) উক্ত বিক্রয়লব্ধ অর্থের নীট পরিমাণ লিপিবদ্ধ করিয়া বন্ডের বিপরীতে সমন্বয় করা হইবে এবং বন্ড সম্পূর্ণ মিটাইবার পর উদ্বৃত্ত, যদি থাকে, তাহা ধারা ২০১ এ বিধৃত পদ্ধতিতে ব্যবস্থিত হইবে।
(৪) পণ্যের কোন হস্তান্তর অথবা স্বত্ব-নিয়োগ উহার উপর পাওনা আদায়ের জন্য যথাযথ কর্মকর্তাকে উপরে বর্ণিত পদ্ধতি অনুযায়ী কার্যক্রম গ্রহণ হইতে নিবৃত্ত করিতে পারিবে না।

Customs Duty: Failure to pay demanded duties or other government dues enables the appropriate officer to take recovery actions.
Recovery methods include executing bonds, seizing warehoused goods, or seizing machinery and other property belonging to the defaulter.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer is empowered to initiate recovery proceedings, including the seizure of goods and assets, against owners who fail to pay required dues.
The officer must provide immediate written notice to the owner upon the seizure of any goods or property.
The officer is responsible for adjusting the proceeds of a sale against the bond and ensuring that any surplus is handled according to established legal procedures.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: Goods stored in a warehouse are subject to seizure if the owner fails to satisfy outstanding customs claims.
Seized goods may be sold to recover debts if the owner does not fulfill the claim within a specified period following the issuance of a formal notice.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal framework for the recovery of unpaid duties, including the authority to seize property and sell goods to satisfy outstanding government claims.
Any transfer of ownership or assignment of goods does not exempt the property from recovery actions taken under the authority of this Act.

Bonded Warehouse Operation: A bond register must be maintained for all bonds executed for customs duties related to warehoused goods.

The register must record all mandatory information prescribed under the law, or alternatively, follow the format specified by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or other designated customs officials for special bonded warehouses.
Customs Duty: The register is required to track bonds executed specifically for customs duties applicable to warehoused goods.
Commissioner of Customs: This authority is empowered to prescribe the form and manner of the bond register specifically for special bonded warehouses.
Bond Cancellation: A bond may be declared discharged and cancelled by the appropriate officer once all goods have been cleared for home consumption or export, or otherwise accounted for, and all outstanding dues have been settled.
Upon cancellation, the bond instrument shall be returned to the person who executed it or the person entitled to receive it upon their request.

Customs Act 1969: This act empowers the appropriate customs official to initiate recovery procedures for outstanding government dues, including unpaid customs duties, regulatory duties, penalties, and amounts owed under bonds or other legal instruments.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the authority to seize, hold, or auction the goods of a debtor, and may issue notices to third parties holding the debtor's funds to recover unpaid government dues.
The officer is empowered to initiate the recovery of outstanding dues through administrative actions against the debtor's assets, including excise-liable goods or bank accounts.

When direct recovery methods are insufficient, the officer can issue a certificate of outstanding dues to the District Collector or a designated Certificate Officer for recovery as arrears of land revenue.
Customs Authority: The customs authority is empowered to withhold the clearance of goods belonging to a debtor from ports, airports, or bonded warehouses until the outstanding government dues are fully paid.
Value Added Tax: Appropriate officers may instruct Value Added Tax officials to seize and sell equipment, machinery, or excise-liable goods owned by the debtor to recover unpaid customs-related government dues.
Public Demands Recovery Act 1913: The government may appoint officers under this act to function as Certificate Officers for the collection of outstanding customs-related dues that have been certified for recovery as public demands.
Scheduled Bank: Upon receiving a written notice from an appropriate officer, a scheduled bank is required to freeze or restrict the operation of a debtor's account to secure the payment of outstanding government dues.

static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
112. Procedure on failure to pay duty, etc.- 4[(1) If any owner fails to pay any sum demanded under section 111, the appropriate officer may either proceed upon the bond executed under 86 or as prescribed by rules made under this Act or cause such portion of the owners goods in the warehouse or any plant or machinery or equipment used for the manufacture of goods or any other goods and properties belonging to such persons to be detained as he may consider adequate to recover the demand, and the notice in writing for such detention, shall immediately be given to the owner.]
(2) In case the demand is not discharged within fifteen days of the date of such notice, the goods so detained may be sold.
(3) The net proceeds of any such sale shall be entered upon and adjusted against the bond and the surplus if any remaining after full satisfaction of the bond shall be disposed of in the manner provided in section 201.
(4) No transfer or assignment of the goods shall prevent the appropriate officer from proceeding against such goods in the manner above provided, for any amount due thereon.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: If the owner fails to pay any sum demanded by the customs authority regarding bonded goods, they are subject to enforcement actions such as bond recovery, detention of warehouse goods, or seizure of manufacturing assets.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer has the authority to recover outstanding duties by enforcing bonds, detaining the owner's goods or equipment, and ultimately selling detained assets if the demand remains unpaid after the specified period.
The officer's right to pursue recovery against goods is not affected by any subsequent transfer or assignment of those goods by the owner.
Warehouse: Goods stored within the warehouse are subject to detention and potential sale by the customs officer if the owner fails to discharge financial demands.
Detained Goods: If a financial demand issued to the owner remains unpaid for the prescribed period following a notice of detention, the goods may be sold to recover the amount due.
The proceeds from the sale of detained goods are used to satisfy the bond obligation, and any surplus funds are managed according to the provisions of the Customs Act.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal framework for the recovery of unpaid duties, including procedures for bond enforcement and the sale of detained property.

114. Register of bonds.- (1) A register shall be kept of all bonds entered into for customs-duties on warehoused goods, and entry shall be made in such register of all particulars required by section 113 to be specified 3[ , or in the case of Special Bonded warehouse entry shall be made in a register to be prescribed by the 4[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board].]
(2) When such register shows that the whole of the goods covered by any bond have been cleared for home-consumption or export, or otherwise duly accounted for, and when all amounts due on account of such goods have been paid, the appropriate officer shall cancel such bond as discharged in full, and shall on demand deliver the cancelled bond to the person who executed it or who is entitled to receive it.

Warehoused Goods: A register must be maintained to record all bonds executed for the payment of customs duties concerning warehoused goods.
Special Bonded Warehouse: For special bonded warehouses, entries must be made in a register specifically prescribed by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or another Commissioner authorized by the Board.
Commissioner of Customs: This official is empowered to prescribe the register format used for recording entries related to special bonded warehouses.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: Once a bond is fully accounted for through home consumption, export, or other legal clearance, and all associated dues are paid, this officer is responsible for canceling the bond as discharged.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to designate which Commissioners of Customs may authorize registers for special bonded warehouses.
